## Natural history notes

A small tiger moth characterized by bright orange to yellow-orange wings, a fuzzy body, and a delicate resting posture, with darker markings sometimes present along the wings or body. In Florida, the Orange Virbia Moth is found in open and semi-open habitats such as pine flatwoods, fields, roadsides, gardens, forest edges, and grassy or weedy areas with low vegetation. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on low herbaceous plants and leaf litter, helping transfer ground-layer plant material into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
